x: While Jon Ridgeon was running the B hurdles at the Parcelforce Games, and Mike Edwards was getting over 5.20, and Lenny Paul, Fred Salle and new signing Ikem Billy were in action, a member with a few more years services than those was also putting in an effort along the Crystal Palace home straight.
New member Ikem Billy placed 5th in the Welsh Games at Cwmbran on July 14th in 1:50.2 but just look who came home in last place - Billy Konchella - destined to be World Champion six weeks later!
Ikem Billy had a 1:47.49 indoor 800m in 1991, but not as a Belgravian, and this time put him 13th in the UK. John Regis's 31.99 for 300 metres was also a European Best.
- Ikem Billy's 8th in the ''Nationals'' in 1:50.40, 4th with 1:48.58 in a scorcher at the ''TSB'' won in 1:45.91 and pacemaker to Noureddine Morceli's 1,000m world record.

We were already changing events for athletes in an attempt to recover points and while Steve Halliday acquitted himself well with a 3rd spot in the 5000m; Ikem Billy showed that he had not recovered from injury in a lack-lustre 1500m.
Ikem Billy looked to have the 800 metres won but was pipped by Nick Pearson. He made amends in the 'B' 400 running steadily and moving from last at 200 metres to hit the front 5 metres out.

Ikem Billy won the 'B' invitation 800 metres in 1:48.54 from Tirelli of Italy but our man from the Wirrall's fastest time at this point had come in an event at Wythenshaw on May 20th when the first ten hit 1:50 or better.
Ikem Billy, not at his best due to injury problems, set off looking every inch a middle-distance man, trailing the field by a long way at the 200.
John Gladwin remained sidelined with niggling injuries and the after effects of M.E. while Ikem Billy added to our woes by reporting injured and looked doubtful for the whole season.
The long relay looked better on paper, especially as we searched the crowd and press-ganged Ikem Billy who claimed not to have touched a track since Budapest.
